brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Tower occupies two levels: base pieces at level 0 (0,0,0 / 0,1,0 / 0,2,0) and upper pieces at level 1 (-1,1,1 / -1,2,1 / 0,1,1 / 0,2,1) linked via snaps, capped and bolted.

Two notch drawer frames: notch:0#-1,1#notch0 and notch:0#-1,2#notch0 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) each provides a pull-out drawer between adjacent tower cells; check_build shows 2 drawers and STABILITY_TIP warning accounted for.
Compact footprint ~ 3 cells tall, two-storey, open faces capped, joints locked, stable (meshClash clear).

finish.summary: Built a two-storey tower (5 bases level 0-1 plus 2 upper full cells) with two notch drawer frames serving as drawers on the front face, capped and joint-bolted.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
